explanation:
[EFFECT] Hour of day has a strongly non-monotonic, two-peak effect. Demand is heavily suppressed in the early-morning hours (0–5), reaching its lowest point around 4 a.m. (contribution near –2.8). It then rises sharply to a morning peak at 8 a.m. (~+1.1), dips slightly mid-morning, and climbs again to the highest positive contributions at 5–6 p.m. (hours 17–18, ~+1.2 to +1.3), before declining again after 10 p.m. and turning slightly negative at midnight.
[IMPORTANCE] This is by far the strongest feature (importance 0.889); its effect dwarfs every other feature in the model.
[RECOMMENDATION] Hour of day and temperature are by far the two strongest drivers of predicted demand, so operational planning — such as bike redistribution and staffing — should be tightly organised around the two daily rush-hour peaks (around 8 a.m. and 5–6 p.m.) and scaled up noticeably in mild to warm weather while scaling back during cold spells or the early hours of the morning.
